duration.$comment: A duration is either a string <number><unit> with unit ns, us, ms, s, m or h ("30s", "1.5m"; "0" or "none" disables the timeout), or the integer 0, which also disables it. The pattern applies only to strings and minimum/maximum only to numbers, so every other number is rejected.

location.description: Where the error was found: the parts of its location that are set, or null when none is.

manifest_location.description: Where discovery found a manifest, without an absolute path.

file.description: The manifest file relative to the search path, '/'-separated: <file>, or <directory>/<file> for a manifest in an immediate subdirectory. Never absolute (no leading /, \ or drive such as C:/), never with a . or .. segment.

search_path.description: The search path that reached the manifest first; the installation's directory has no index.

index.description: The search path's position among the non-empty entries of its origin, as given, from 0; an entry that repeats an earlier path still counts.

origin.description: Where the search path comes from: the caller's paths, the configuration's modules.search_paths, the environment variable (PRAENORA_MODULE_PATH or PRAENORA_PROVIDER_PATH), or the installation's directory.

engine.description: The engine object of the provider's manifest.

minor.description: The minor version the provider offers.

source_location.description: A file (UTF-8 path), a 1-based line and column (columns count bytes; a column only with a line) and a JSON pointer into the document.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC time with exactly 9 fractional digits.

run-record.description: What a run used (the hashed reproducibility section) and how it went (execution).

final_status.description: The final status snapshot (a status-snapshot document), written when the run ends. Its error records name the run's directories by placeholders, as execution.error does.

inputs.description: What each replay source (observation-csv) found in its data, by input; a json-document input has no entry. Outside the hashed section: the numbers follow from the file's bytes and the configuration, which the fingerprint covers.

^(?!(inputs|outputs)$)[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: rows_total: the rows of the input's observation CSV; rows_before_start: those whose time is before run.time.start, which the replay never delivers.

isolation.description: How each step's module instance was isolated, by step, every field resolved: mode in-process (in the runtime's process) or process (in a module host), whether its module host shared compiled models, and its sandbox profile. Outside the hashed section: it does not change the fingerprint.

sandbox.description: The sandbox profile of the step's module host: none, or restricted.

share_compiled_models.description: Whether the step's module host shared compiled models with the other sharing steps' module hosts.

manifests.description: Where each manifest of the run was found, relative to a search path named by its origin and index, never by an absolute path. Outside the hashed section: it does not change the fingerprint.

services.description: Where the provider manifest of each runtime service of the run was found, by <name>@<major>.

steps.description: Where the module manifest of each step was found, by step.

overrides.description: The run settings the caller overrode (CLI flags or API options); empty when none.

status.description: The run's status: running from its start, then how it ended.

validation.description: Whether payloads were validated against their message types (strict) or not (off, for performance measurements).

catalog.description: Digest of every catalog entry used, by id@version.

services.description: Every runtime service a provider serves to the run, by <name>@<major>.
The keys of the top-level services that the step's module may use, sorted.

ticks.description: The run's tick count; null when the run lasts until its replay inputs are exhausted.

info.description: The control and status API of the Praenora runtime, served by praenora run --listen (run mode: the one run of the process, id 1) and praenora serve (serve mode: runs opened on request from configurations under a configuration root). Over a Unix socket every request has the read and control scopes; over TCP without tokens only the read scope; over TCP with tokens, every request but GET /v0/health needs "Authorization: Bearer <token>". TCP requests need a Host header that names the server. A known path with another method answers 405 with Allow. Every POST, stop included, needs Content-Type: application/json (stop's body may be empty), else 415. Bodies are compact JSON in UTF-8; errors are error documents. The runtime's schemas below are JSON Schema draft-07, embedded with their own $schema and $id.
info.title: Praenora control API
